problem: Choose compatible giver and receiver grasps and a mutually reachable exchange pose for robot-to-robot object handover.
contribution: A learning-free geometric/probabilistic grasp detector based on locally fitted superquadrics, followed by reachability-aware grasp-pair and exchange-pose selection.
algorithm: Initialize multiple ellipsoids using K-means partitions and an additional whole-cloud initialization; fit hidden superquadrics with a mixture/outlier model and optimization-based Gibbs sampling. Rank parallel-jaw grasp candidates using geometry/contact/center-of-mass criteria. Select collision-compatible grasp pairs and an exchange pose maximizing reachable receiver grasps using precomputed 6D reachability SDFs.
observations: Fused object point clouds from two calibrated depth sensors, known gripper geometry and robot reachability maps. Assumes an initially planar supporting surface and reconstructs missing bottom geometry.
actions: Giver grasp, exchange pose and receiver grasp pose. Low-level execution and physical release behavior are distinct from the geometric planner.
embodiment_and_data: Real experiments use two Franka arms and depth cameras; grasp detection uses two Azure Kinects, handover uses Primesense RGB-D and L515. No learned training dataset is needed. Implemented in Python on Ryzen 9 5950X.
experiments: Isolated and packed-scene grasp tests and a handover test with six objects, five initial-position attempts per object, total 30 handovers. Handover success requires the receiver to remove the object from the giver workspace.
baselines: Published RIMEDNet results on two objects; these are not a matched rerun on the same six-object protocol. Grasp comparisons use additional methods; individual numeric grasp results were not extracted in this review.

quantitative_result.value: Handover HSR 83.3% over 30 trials; the exact integer success numerator is not printed in the examined table. RIMEDNet object-specific reported rates 74.4% and 66.3% use a different object set.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p12 Section5.2 denominator and p13 Table3
quantitative_result.comparability: Cross-paper object/protocol mismatch; not evidence of Explorer performance.

limitations: Relative object movement in the giver invalidates the receiver grasp computed before pickup and causes drops. Assumes rigid geometric representations, uniform-density center-of-mass approximation, calibrated depth and two capable arms. Physical passing optimization is future work despite an executed handover pipeline; planning success is not a verified release-safety argument.
code_and_license: Primary article and fulltext verified. Executable source repository and code license were not established in this review; do not copy implementation under an assumed article license.
hardware_adaptation: Use as a planning baseline and motivation for observing object movement during handover. SO-101/ROSMASTER grippers, arm DOFs, calibration and RGB-only observability differ. Require independent grip/ownership evidence before any giver release; geometric reachability alone cannot authorize motion.
algorithm_detail: The superquadric fitter treats much of the cloud as outliers so several initializations recover local graspable parts. The exchange selector transforms receiver candidate grasps by the giver/object pose and queries the receiver SDF. Reachability SDFs omit some dynamic inter-arm collision checks, so these need a separate check.
integration_contract: Inputs: calibrated object cloud, explicit giver/object/receiver transforms, measured gripper widths and robot-specific reachability model. Outputs: ranked pose pairs with frame IDs and separate collision/reachability validity. Never convert these directly into a release command.
license_evidence: Code license UNKNOWN; article DOI and publisher PDF are archival references, not an executable-code grant.
required_experiments: Matched object/pose trials against a simpler object-relative geometric baseline; rigid-versus-slip perturbations; failed grasp and receiver-observation ablations; report attempted handovers, drops, interventions, unknown outcomes and full release evidence separately.
difference_from_explorer: Explorer's no-actuator handover FSM is engineering glue, not this paper's grasp planner, physical validation or a novel handover method.
